h1: Royal Twins Palace Hotel Pattaya — A Big Tower in the City Centre a 5-Minute Walk from Walking Street
intro: Picture waking up, opening the curtains and stepping onto your balcony to see the Gulf of Thailand stretched out in front of you — then, come evening, walking down just a few minutes to reach Pattaya Beach and Walking Street. Royal Twins Palace Hotel is a long-established 4-star high-rise in South Pattaya whose main draw is its central-city location and the sea views from the balconies · It's a roughly 15-storey building with around 350 rooms on Pattaya 2nd Road, and a lot of people choose it because it's about a 5-minute walk to Pattaya Beach and Walking Street, close to Royal Garden Plaza and Ripley's · There's an outdoor pool, a kids' pool, a pool bar, a Thai massage spa and a breakfast buffet, plus free parking and free Wi-Fi · Prices start at about ฿1,200/night · It scores 7.4 from 358 reviews on Booking.com, with location rated as high as 8.8 — and to be straight with you, it's an older building that was once luxurious, so the charm is in the location and value rather than how new it feels

body.html: Who Royal Twins Palace is right for — if we had to sum it up as briefly as possible, Royal Twins Palace Hotel is a hotel for people who want to stay "right in the middle of Pattaya" with everything within walking distance, without paying luxury beachfront prices · It's not a brand-new resort where everything is spotless, and it's not a small boutique that sells quiet · Instead it's a roughly 15-storey high-rise with around 350 rooms in South Pattaya, a place that was once a well-known luxury hotel in its era and today positions itself as a 4-star hotel selling location and value above all · From real reviews on Booking.com, Agoda and TripAdvisor, the people it suits best are couples and groups of friends who come to Pattaya for the nightlife, travellers who want a room with a sea-view balcony on a modest budget, and people who drive themselves and need free parking in the city centre · Another group that finds it worthwhile are travellers who use the hotel simply as a base for going out, because staying here means you barely have to plan transport at all — everything is within walking distance or a short ride away · The group it may not suit are people who expect a flawless new room in every detail, or those looking for the private, resort-style calm, because this is an older hotel right in the entertainment district, with both tour groups and plenty of buzz · Frankly, if you set your expectations to match the words "older building, prime location, good value," Royal Twins Palace does its job well — but if you expect five-star, brand-new luxury, you'll run into a few things you don't love

Location and getting around — this is, without question, Royal Twins Palace's number-one selling point, and the reason its "location" category on Booking.com scores as high as 8.8, clearly ahead of the other categories · The hotel sits on Pattaya 2nd Road in Nongprue subdistrict, Bang Lamung district, Chon Buri, in the South Pattaya zone that is the city's entertainment hub · The thing many people choose it for is that it's about a 5-minute walk to Pattaya Beach and Beach Road, and a little further to the mouth of Walking Street, the pedestrian street that's Pattaya's highlight · Within walking distance of the hotel you'll find Royal Garden Plaza, Ripley's Believe It or Not, the night market and plenty of restaurants and convenience stores to choose from · For getting further afield: Central Pattaya mall and Terminal 21 are about a 10–15 min drive, Jomtien Beach about a 5–10 min drive, and U-Tapao Airport (UTP) around 40 km or a 40–50 min drive · One thing reviews note is that if you're not driving yourself, getting to other spots means relying on songthaews or Grab, which can take a bit longer in the busy evening hours · But for people focused on exploring the South Pattaya zone and the beach, this location plus free parking is a genuine advantage, and it's why people choose to stay here again and again even though the building has some age on it

"The location is the best part — a few minutes' walk to the beach and Walking Street · We got a room with a balcony looking out at the sea for under two thousand, which is great value for Pattaya, even if the building is a bit dated."

Room types and decor — Royal Twins Palace has around 350 rooms in total spread across a roughly 15-storey high-rise, split into several tiers · It starts with the Superior Room, the standard room, then moves up to the Deluxe Room, which is more spacious with better in-room amenities · And there are 1-bedroom and 2-bedroom Suites for families or groups who want more space and a separate living area · Something many people like is that every room has a private balcony, and most look out over the Gulf of Thailand sea view or the city view — a detail you don't often find in hotels at this price · Most rooms are fairly spacious, with a seating area and a desk, plus air conditioning, a flat-screen TV with cable channels, a fridge or minibar, and an en-suite bathroom with a shower · Plenty of reviews agree that the rooms are spacious and the sea-view balconies are lovely, especially on the higher floors · But to be straight about it, the most common observation is that the rooms and furniture look dated, in line with the building's age — the decor is in an older hotel style, some rooms are fairly dim from yellow lighting, some spots show signs of wear, and some bathrooms are small with weak water pressure · For people who care about the view and the space, you should request a higher-floor sea-view room when you book, because that's where this hotel's rooms do their best — and anyone wanting something pristine and new should set their expectations to match the phrase "older hotel, good location"

Facilities, pool and spa — for a hotel at this level, Royal Twins Palace covers the facilities reasonably well · The highlight is the outdoor pool, which many reviews say is a decent size, letting guests cool off after a full day of sightseeing, along with a separate kids' pool and a pool bar that put families with young children more at ease · There's also a Thai massage spa, a jacuzzi/whirlpool, a coffee shop and a restaurant for people who want to relax in the hotel · For basic services, there's a 24-hour front desk, free parking, free Wi-Fi, a lift, laundry service and a shared computer · To be straight about it, the pool and spa are more in the older-hotel mould than new-resort luxury, and the gym is fairly small · Another thing reviews mention is the lift — because it's a 15-storey building with a lot of rooms, you may sometimes have to wait a while for the lift when everyone comes down at once · Overall, the facilities match the concept of "has everything, good enough, good value" more than being something you come here specifically for

Food and breakfast — the hotel has its own restaurant and coffee shop, and the thing that gets fairly consistent praise in reviews is the breakfast buffet — many reviews say breakfast is varied and well put together for the price, with both Thai and international options, which is more than you'd expect for a hotel at this price · For other meals, the hotel's location helps a lot, because step out the door and you're surrounded by the restaurants, street-food stalls and convenience stores of South Pattaya, so many people choose to eat out rather than have every meal in the hotel — which is part of the charm of staying in the city centre · One thing some reviews note is that the dining options in the hotel beyond breakfast are fairly limited, so if you want a varied dinner you usually have to head out · But in a city like Pattaya, where you can find tasty, budget-friendly food on every street corner, that's barely an issue · In short, breakfast is something the hotel does well and good value, while the location around the hotel handles the other meals

Service — service is an area where real reviews are mixed · On the praise side, many reviews say the staff are friendly and helpful, especially with travel advice and calling cars, and the 24-hour front desk means guests arriving late or coming back late from a night out are looked after around the clock · The "staff" category on Booking.com scores around 7.7, which is okay · But to be straight about it, some voices in the reviews say some staff have limited English, and the check-in–check-out process at certain times feels like an old system and takes a while, especially when tour groups arrive at the same time · This is something you'll find at large older hotels that take tour groups, and it's not a problem that keeps most people from coming back · Overall the service is at an acceptable level for the price, and compared with what they pay, most people feel they're looked after well enough

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — pulling it together from Booking.com, Agoda and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a central South Pattaya location a 5-minute walk to the beach and Walking Street (location category 8.8), spacious rooms with sea-view balconies especially on the higher floors, a large pool with a kids' pool and pool bar, a varied breakfast buffet, free parking in the city centre, and value for money compared with the price · On the observation side: the most talked-about thing is the building and rooms being dated with age — the furniture, the decor and the in-room lighting look older, and some spots show signs of wear · Next is waiting a long time for the lift when it's busy because it's a high-rise with a lot of rooms, some bathrooms being small with weak water pressure, some staff having limited English, and the buzz of the tour groups and entertainment district around the hotel that can mean some noise on certain nights · Most of these criticisms are predictable for an older hotel in the city centre and can be solved by choosing the right room and setting the right expectations, rather than being a major problem that keeps people from coming back

"Spacious room, a lovely sea-view balcony, breakfast was better than the price suggested · My only gripe is the dated building and the long lift wait in the morning · But a location like this at this price is hard to find in Pattaya — next time I'll ask for a higher-floor sea-view room."

Price comparison and value — the starting price for a Superior room is about ฿1,200/night at normal rates (roughly 35–45 dollars as shown on many platforms) · Deluxe rooms and higher-floor sea-view rooms move up to around ฿1,500–2,000, and the Suites go higher than that depending on size and season · Over long weekends and high season, prices tend to climb quickly, like other hotels in Pattaya · Compared with hotels in the same area, Royal Twins Palace mainly feels good value in terms of location and room size — you get a spacious room with a sea-view balcony in central South Pattaya, within walking distance of the beach and Walking Street, on a budget several times cheaper than the luxury beachfront hotels · The trade-off is accepting that the building and rooms aren't new · If you plan to use Pattaya for nightlife and beachfront strolls, valuing location and the view over how new the room is, the money you spend here pays off well · But if you're willing to pay more for a pristine new room or a genuine beachfront resort, you may need to step your budget up a level

What to know before you book — there are several things that help make the stay smoother · One, if the view matters to you, request a higher-floor sea-view room when you book, because that's where this hotel's rooms do their best, while garden-view or lower-floor rooms see less · Two, since it's a 15-storey building with a lot of rooms, the lift can take a while in the morning when everyone checks out at once, so allow time if you're in a hurry · Three, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a room that doesn't face the busy side of 2nd Road, because South Pattaya comes alive at night · Four, if you drive yourself, the free parking is an advantage in the city centre — check on the number of available spaces when the hotel is full · Five, set your expectations to "older hotel, good location" rather than a flawless new room, and the experience will match what you get · Six, over long weekends and high season Pattaya fills up fast and prices climb, so book ahead, compare prices across several platforms, and pick free cancellation first if your plans aren't set

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Royal Twins Palace Hotel is the hotel that suits people who want to stay in central South Pattaya, within walking distance of the beach and Walking Street, with a spacious room and a sea-view balcony on a modest budget · A location that scores 8.8, a pool with a kids' pool, a well-put-together breakfast buffet, and free parking in the city centre make it good value in terms of location and price, to the point where finding a rival at the same price isn't easy · If you're looking for a flawless brand-new room in every detail, or a quiet beachfront resort, this may not be the answer, because it's an older building that was once luxurious and shows details that come with age — consider a higher-tier hotel or a resort over on the Jomtien side instead · But for a Pattaya trip focused on sightseeing, walking and location, where you want a sea-view balcony without paying a premium — Royal Twins Palace is a choice that does its job well, and that's why it keeps earning solid review scores from hundreds of guests

honestSummary: Royal Twins Palace Hotel is the best choice for people who want to stay in central South Pattaya, within walking distance of the beach and Walking Street, with a spacious room and a sea-view balcony on a modest budget — location scores 8.8, with a pool, a kids' pool and a well-put-together breakfast buffet · But you have to accept it's an older building that was once luxurious, the rooms and furniture look dated, and the lift can take a while in a 15-storey high-rise
honestChecks: If you want a flawless, pristine new room — this is an older hotel where the furniture and decor look dated, and some rooms are dimly lit → ask for a higher-floor Deluxe sea-view room, or consider a recently renovated hotel if newness matters

If you're a light sleeper and sensitive to noise — South Pattaya is lively at night and the hotel takes tour groups → ask for a room that doesn't face the busy side of 2nd Road, and pick a higher floor to be safe

If you're after the quiet calm of a beachfront resort — this is a high-rise right in the entertainment district, not a place to escape the bustle → consider a resort over on the Jomtien or Na Jomtien side instead

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Royal Twins Palace Hotel Pattaya

faq.q: Where is Royal Twins Palace Hotel · can you walk to Walking Street?
faq.a: The hotel is on Pattaya 2nd Road in Nongprue subdistrict, Bang Lamung district, Chon Buri, in central South Pattaya · It's about a 5-minute walk to Pattaya Beach and Beach Road, and a little further to Walking Street · It's near Royal Garden Plaza and Ripley's · The location category on Booking.com scores as high as 8.8

faq.q: What's the starting price at Royal Twins Palace · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿1,200/night for a Superior room at normal rates · There are Deluxe rooms and higher-floor sea-view rooms around ฿1,500–2,000, and one- to two-bedroom Suites for families · High-season and long-weekend prices climb quickly, so compare across several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Royal Twins Palace right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples and groups of friends who come for the nightlife, travellers who want a room with a sea-view balcony on a modest budget, and people who drive themselves and need free parking in the city centre · It's all about a location within walking distance of the beach and Walking Street · If you're after a pristine new room or the quiet calm of a resort, the Jomtien side may suit you better

faq.q: Does Royal Twins Palace have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — there's a large outdoor pool with a kids' pool and pool bar, plus a Thai massage spa and jacuzzi · The breakfast buffet is something many reviews praise as varied and well put together for the price, with both Thai and international options (depending on the package booked)

faq.q: Is Royal Twins Palace old · what condition are the rooms in?
faq.a: To be straight, it's an older hotel that was once luxurious — the building, furniture and decor look dated, some rooms are dimly lit and some bathrooms are small · But most rooms are spacious with a sea-view balcony, especially on the higher floors · The charm here is in the location and value, not how new it is, so set your expectations to match

faq.q: What are the lift and the noise like at Royal Twins Palace?
faq.a: It's a 15-storey high-rise with a lot of rooms, so in the morning when everyone checks out at once the lift can take a while — allow some time · South Pattaya is lively at night and the hotel takes tour groups, so if you're a light sleeper we'd suggest asking for a higher-floor room that doesn't face the busy side of 2nd Road when you book
